title: Keys aren’t just for lists: reset a form

slides.say: You type a message to Alice, then tap Bob. Your draft is still there, ready to go to the wrong person.
Chat is at the same place in the tree, so React keeps its state. Only the contact prop changed.
Give it a key. A new recipient means a new key, so React recreates Chat from scratch, with all the state below it.
Same trick for a reset button. Bump a version number and pass it as the key. The whole form starts fresh.

slides.text: Keys only need to be unique within the parent. A new key means fresh state.
slides.say: Keys only need to be unique inside their parent. Change the key, and you get fresh state.
